answer: The statistical consequence of omitting a relevant variable from a regression model, when both the omitted variable and its covariance with the included variable are positive, is that the population regression slope on the included variable will be larger than the coefficient in the fuller model. This occurs because the slope in the model omitting the relevant variable incorporates part of the relationship that the omitted variable has with the outcome, leading to an inflated estimate of the effect of the included variable.
